title: Iraq at the World Cup
description: From their sole 1986 appearance to qualifying for 2026 — Iraq's football journey has overcome extraordinary challenges.

questions.q: Iraq made their only World Cup appearance before 2026 in which year?
questions.explain: Iraq competed at the 1986 World Cup in Mexico — their first and only World Cup before 2026. They were eliminated in the group stage, losing all three matches.

questions.q: At the 1986 World Cup, Iraq held which European nation to a 1–1 draw — their only point of the tournament?
questions.explain: Iraq drew 1–1 with Belgium at the 1986 World Cup — earning their only point of the tournament. It was a creditable result against a Belgium side that would finish fourth in the same tournament.

questions.q: Iraq has won the AFC Asian Cup how many times?
questions.explain: Iraq won the AFC Asian Cup in 2007, hosted across four Southeast Asian countries. Beating Saudi Arabia in the final was a moment of national joy during an extraordinarily difficult period in Iraq's history.

questions.q: Iraq's 2007 Asian Cup win was especially significant because it came during which period in the country's history?
options: The Gulf War aftermath of the 1990s
During the Iraq War and intense sectarian violence of the mid-2000s
During international sanctions following the 1990 Kuwait invasion
questions.explain: Iraq's 2007 Asian Cup triumph came while the country was experiencing intense sectarian violence and the aftermath of the Iraq War. Celebrations erupted across Baghdad despite security dangers — the team united a divided nation.

questions.q: Which Iraqi player is regarded as one of the best in Asian football history and played in Europe for multiple clubs?
questions.explain: Younis Mahmoud is Iraq's most iconic modern player — the striker who scored the 2007 Asian Cup final winner against Saudi Arabia. He played his club career mainly in Asia and the Middle East.

questions.q: Iraq qualified for the 2026 World Cup — their first in 40 years. Through which confederation?
questions.explain: Iraq qualified through AFC qualifying for the 2026 World Cup — ending a 40-year absence from the tournament. The expanded 48-team format gave more Asian nations a pathway to qualification.

questions.q: Iraq's national team nicknamed 'Lions of Mesopotamia' is named after which ancient civilisation that flourished in modern-day Iraq?
questions.explain: Iraq are called the Lions of Mesopotamia — a reference to the ancient civilisation of Mesopotamia, centred on modern-day Iraq and considered one of the world's earliest civilisations, founded along the Tigris and Euphrates rivers.

questions.q: Iraq faced significant challenges in qualifying for World Cups due to international sanctions and conflict. Which period saw them banned from international football?
options: 1991–1994 following the Gulf War and UN sanctions
There was no formal ban — they simply failed to qualify
questions.explain: Iraq were never formally banned from international football but faced enormous practical difficulties — including security issues, inability to host matches, and limited training resources — that made World Cup qualification nearly impossible for decades.

questions.q: Which Iraqi forward has been their most prolific scorer in recent AFC qualifying campaigns ahead of 2026?
questions.explain: Aymen Hussein has been Iraq's standout striker in the 2026 qualifying campaign, leading the scoring charts. His club career in the Iraqi league has seen consistent goal-scoring that has translated to international level.

questions.q: Iraq will play 2026 World Cup group stage matches at venues across North America. This will be the first time Iraqi fans can attend matches in a relatively accessible location. Which host country are they least likely to encounter visa difficulties for?
options: All three present similar challenges for Iraqi passport holders
questions.explain: Iraqi passport holders face visa requirements for all three 2026 host nations (USA, Canada and Mexico), but the World Cup typically facilitates easier fan travel. The tournament will nonetheless be a historic opportunity for Iraqi football supporters.
